identity.industry: Defense & Nuclear Inspection Systems / Steel Processing Automation

summary.oneLiner: Admach Systems delivered strong FY26 growth (Revenue +29%, PAT +59%) driven by defense and nuclear orders, with a strategic pivot to 70% in-house manufacturing via recent capex expected to restore EBITDA margins to >20% in FY27. The INR 65 crore order book (executing by Sep-26) and a INR 200+ crore quoted pipeline provide high visibility for crossing INR 100 crore revenue in FY27 and targeting INR 200 crore by FY28.

one-line thesis: Admach Systems delivered strong FY26 growth (Revenue +29%, PAT +59%) driven by defense and nuclear orders, with a strategic pivot to 70% in-house manufacturing via recent capex expected to restore EBITDA margins to >20% in FY27. The INR 65 crore order book (executing by Sep-26) and a INR 200+ crore quoted pipeline provide high visibility for crossing INR 100 crore revenue in FY27 and targeting INR 200 crore by FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 68.91cr (+29% YoY); EBITDA INR 13.69cr (~19.9% margin, down QoQ due to project mix & commissioning delays); PAT INR 10.01cr (+59% YoY); Order Book INR 65cr (100% execution expected by Sep-26); Net Debt: Low (Receivables inflated to INR 31cr due to logistics delays/shipping constraints, not credit risk). One-offs: Lower effective tax rate (~17% annualized) due to accelerated depreciation on new capex; Gross margin compression (33% to 29%) attributed to high-steel-sector contribution in prior year vs diversified lower-margin mix currently.
guidance: Revenue: Cross INR 100cr in FY27, target INR 200cr by FY28; Margin: Target >20% EBITDA in FY27 driven by backward integration; Order Inflow: INR 200cr+ quoted pipeline with 60-65% conversion expected; Capex: Near completion, final machines arriving July 2026.
order book & pipeline: INR 65 crores total; Includes INR 10cr from Nuclear Fuel Complex (execution by Sep-26); Mixed bag across Steel, Defense, Nuclear, Packaging; Current dispatches delayed slightly due to global shipping constraints (resolved via South Africa route).
segment / subsidiary detail: Steel (Long products ~70-75%, Flat ~25-30%): Chamfering, straightening, bright bar finishing; Defense: X-ray/NDT for missile shells (155mm Howitzer), aerospace components; Nuclear: Fuel handling systems (NFC orders); Exports: 28 countries, direct to US (6 pipe projects) and Brazil/Taiwan/Korea defense deals.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 'Bright Bar' and superfinishing equipment (downstream of rolling mills); Pre-rolling billet conditioning lines (partnership with Braun Machinefabrik, Austria) adding INR 30-40cr potential per plant vs INR 50cr post-rolling; Nuclear pipeline of 4-8 additional projects beyond current INR 10cr order; Direct exports under own brand increasing vs partner-led.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin compressed to 29% (from 33%) due to project mix shift away from high-margin steel projects (Tata Steel FY24) to diversified base; Backward integration (CNC laser, press brake, tapping) shifting outsourcing ratio from 70/30 to 30/70 (in-house), expected to add 300-400 bps to EBITDA margins starting Q1 FY27.
capex / expansion: Recent installation of CNC laser cutting, press brake, and automatic tapping machines; Final 1-2 machines expected July 2026; Total facility capacity now scaled to support INR 200cr revenue (vs current ~INR 70cr run-rate); Land acquired for future Unit 2/3 expansion.
capital allocation: Organic capacity expansion prioritized; Working capital requirement estimated at INR 20-30cr for INR 200cr revenue scale; No M&A mentioned; Focus on reducing job-work payouts to improve cash conversion.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on large single-order dispatches (INR 15-16cr units) impacting quarterly lumpiness; Receivable days elevated (150-160 days) due to logistics/shipping delays rather than customer credit, though cash flow timing affected; Dependency on government capex cycles (Defense/Nuclear/Steel); Project-based revenue recognition leading to volatility.
management quality / tone: Highly confident on growth trajectory ('sky is the limit'); Transparent about margin dip being temporary (commissioning phase); Aggressive on defense/nuclear opportunities citing 'Make in India' mandates; Pragmatic on logistics challenges with solutions implemented.
non-obvious takeaways: Revenue recognition tied strictly to dispatch (ex-works), causing inventory-to-revenue lumps; Tax rate anomaly (9% H2 vs 25% historical) clarified as benefit from accelerated depreciation on new capex under IT Act, not cash withholding; Defense applications include full-shell X-ray inspection for live ammunition (Brazil/Taiwan/Korea exports), a high-barrier niche; 'Bright Bar' demand driven by automotive shift away from black bars.

themes.title: Defence indigenization & order-book visibility
themes.need: Indigenization mandates (IDDM / Atmanirbhar / DcPP) plus multi-year order books make domestic defence the cleanest revenue-conversion theme - across electronics, drones, simulators, explosives/munitions and precision systems. BEL guides >INR55k cr FY27 inflow (~INR30k cr QRSAM pending CCS clearance, guided by September) on a INR72,258cr order book; HAL book ~INR2.55 lakh cr; SOLARINDS defence revenue +94% to INR2,634cr FY26, guided >INR4,500cr FY27 on an ~INR18,000cr defence order book (Bhargavastra counter-drone trials completing CY2026); DATAPATTNS inflows strong; BHARATFORG/BEML add land-systems and platforms.
themes.driver: Backlog-to-revenue conversion underway; BEL's QRSAM CCS clearance (guided by Sep-2026, ~INR30k cr of the FY27 inflow guide) is the load-bearing near-term catalyst; fresh MoD orders + emergency procurement; HAL LCA Mk-1A ramp (gated on GE engines).

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
